name: brain tumours overview
title: Suspected brain tumour: progressive symptoms and raised intracranial pressure prompt a contrast MRI; metastasis is treated by resection and radiation, a glioma by its grade (an enhancing high-grade glioma is treated at once, a non-enhancing low-grade glioma can be watched), and primary CNS lymphoma is suspected in the immunosuppressed

root.title: Could it be a brain TUMOUR? The red flag is PROGRESSIVE symptoms
lines: • raised pressure: ↓ consciousness · headache, nausea, vomiting · Cushing response · papilledema (LATE) · herniation
• headache: persistent, progressive, worse lying down and in the morning, wakes from sleep, worse with cough or Valsalva
• focal deficit · mental status change (mistaken for depression or dementia) · seizures, especially focal
• CONTRAST MRI (gadolinium) = test of choice · CT only WITH contrast · tissue diagnosis still needed
• steroids for brain swelling · anti-seizure drugs only once there is a seizure

lines: gliomas are the most common primary
